lens: Items and prices against build/draft_doc.json, ingredient names and how complete the descriptions are (with public_components), section flow for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The descriptions are the weakest part, and the proposal presents the gaps as a rule rather than flagging them. 5 of 14 items have no description at all: Brut Rosé, Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP and Dry Cider's real content. The descriptions that remain have been cut down to fragments that tell the guest almost nothing: 'Toasty', 'Hop-forward', 'Sparkling', 'Dry red'. No beer shows an ABV, no wine shows a region, and no spirit shows an age or brand. The printed menu does not flag any of these as missing_ingredients. The gaps are only mentioned in the proposal's open items. On top of that, a Mexican cantina's menu opens with a Manhattan, and the agave spirits are left at the bottom of the right column with no descriptions, so the reading path undercuts what the venue is.
problems: Items and prices: all 14 items and all 14 prices match the draft exactly (Manhattan 15, Margarita 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Dry Cider 8). Nothing is invented or dropped, and the sub-groups are kept.

public_components is handled correctly: Aromatic Bitters is hidden on the Manhattan, and the garnish is shown as cocktail cherry. The Old Fashioned (house_recipe=false) shows ingredient names only, which is correct.

The 'drop the echo' rule removes descriptions without flagging them. Brut Rosé and all 3 spirits show nothing, even though the draft gives each a description line. The menu shows no missing_ingredients flag for these items, and it asks for no ABV, region, age or brand.

The cut-down descriptions no longer meet criterion 8. Beer: 'Toasty' and 'Hop-forward' give no style word in the description and no ABV. Wine: 'Dry red' and 'Dry white' give no region. Cider: 'Sparkling' alone. Cutting 'Bright and citrus-forward' from the Margarita removes the only line on the page that sounds appetising.
The syrup is named inconsistently: 'demerara syrup' on the Daiquiri but 'demerara' on the Old Fashioned (the draft component for both is Demerara Syrup).

Flow: Cider is moved from its draft position to sit under Beer. That is a reasonable grouping, but it leaves the columns as Cocktails/Beer/Cider against Wine/Spirits, so the agave spirits the venue should lead with come last and without descriptions. The first thing a guest reads at a Mexican cantina is a rye Manhattan.

Visual rhythm: the right column alternates between blocks with descriptions (by-the-glass wine) and blocks of bare names (Sparkling, Agave, Brandy). It reads like two different list systems stitched together.

Price format is consistent: integers with no $, right-aligned in tabular figures on the 320 px column. But short names give a long hop with no leader or row rule: 'Brut Rosé' to 13, 'Amber Lager' to 7, and 'Dry Cider' to 8 run past about 50% of the column. Because the measure is short, association still passes, but only just.
Taglines: 'Good drinks / Good people' is generic brand voice and states no item fact, so it passes. '& Cocktail Bar / Iowa City, Iowa' describes the venue, not an item, so it passes.
fixes: Put the draft descriptions back wherever cutting them left nothing or only one adjective. If a line repeats the item name, rewrite it from draft facts rather than dropping it (e.g. Brut Rosé 'Dry sparkling rosé', Dry Cider 'Dry, sparkling').

Mark every beer (ABV), wine (region), tequila and Cognac (brand/age) visibly as missing_ingredients in the proposal and doc. Ask the Coordinator for the data before release, and do not ship lines that are just empty space.
In Cocktails, lead with the Margarita (a draft-order swap within Classics, with no content change) so a Mexican cantina's first read is agave, not rye.
Use one term for Demerara Syrup on both the Daiquiri and the Old Fashioned, and put 'Bright and citrus-forward' back on the Margarita as a second line if the measure allows.

For rows where the name is short and the price is far away (Brut Rosé, Amber Lager, Dry Cider), shorten the name-to-price hop. Pull prices in to a narrower price column, or add a fine dotted leader in the ivory tint.
